data.title: Thin-File Identity Clustering — Shared Address, Phone, or Device Across New Applicants
data.description: Detects clusters of thin-file credit applicants sharing physical addresses, phone numbers, or device fingerprints — a hallmark indicator of synthetic identity ring activity. Fraud rings fabricate multiple synthetic identities that share infrastructure (mailing addresses, burner phones, devices used for applications). When 3+ new applicants with thin credit files (< 12 months history, < 3 tradelines) share an address, phone, or device within a 180-day window, this indicates coordinated identity fabrication rather than coincidental overlap. The Federal Reserve identifies address and device clustering as primary synthetic identity detection signals.

detection.condition: count(distinct applicant_id) by shared_attribute >= 3 where shared_attribute in (address, phone, device_fingerprint) within 180 days AND selection_thin_file

enrichment_required.source: Credit bureau inquiry — months since oldest tradeline
Credit bureau inquiry — number of active tradelines

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Thin-File Identity Clustering")`
`comment("Detects 3+ thin-file applicants sharing address, phone, or device")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:account_onboarding
  credit_history_months<12 tradeline_count<3
| stats dc(applicant_id) AS applicant_count,
        values(applicant_id) AS applicants,
        values(phone) AS phones,
        values(device_fingerprint) AS devices,
        values(ssn_hash) AS ssn_hashes,
        min(application_date) AS first_app,
        max(application_date) AS last_app
  BY address
| where applicant_count >= 3
| eval days_span = round((strptime(last_app, "%Y-%m-%d") - strptime(first_app, "%Y-%m-%d")) / 86400)
| where days_span <= 180
| eval shared_attribute = "address"
| table address, applicant_count, applicants, phones, devices,
        ssn_hashes, first_app, last_app, days_span
| sort - applicant_count
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Thin-File Identity Clustering
-- Detects 3+ thin-file applicants sharing address within 180 days
SELECT
  a.address,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.applicant_id) AS applicant_count,
  STRING_AGG(a.applicant_id, ', ') AS applicants,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT a.phone, ', ') AS phones,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT a.device_fingerprint, ', ') AS devices,
  MIN(a.application_date) AS first_application,
  MAX(a.application_date) AS last_application,
  DATEDIFF(DAY, MIN(a.application_date), MAX(a.application_date)) AS days_span
FROM credit_applications a
WHERE a.credit_history_months < 12
  AND a.tradeline_count < 3
  AND a.application_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -180, CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY a.address
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.applicant_id) >= 3
ORDER BY applicant_count DESC

references: Federal Reserve, Synthetic Identity Fraud in the U.S. Payment System (2024)
OCC, Comptroller's Handbook: Credit Card Lending — Address Clustering
Socure, Synthetic Identity Detection via Graph Analytics (2025)
falsepositives: Shared housing (college dormitories, military barracks, assisted living facilities)
Family members with thin credit files applying from the same household
New immigrants sharing temporary housing while establishing credit
